request.description: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment.

A decider who does not yet support the decision gives it full support.

Whoever holds a concern's information starts the remedy; 2 rounds later the concern is resolved.
The person a concern reached starts the remedy on their own side; 2 rounds later it is resolved.
Whoever holds a resolved concern's information raises a new local concern on the same matter, through the same channel to the same person.
The person a resolved concern reached finds the remedy wanting and reopens it.
Anyone puts a matter before the group while the decision is open or in effect; it stays on the agenda until someone settles it.
Anyone settles one of the matters still open on the group's agenda.
A decider puts a rejected decision back on the table; it is decided again 6 rounds later.
The partnership convenes and holds a meeting to consider activation; it may do this repeatedly during the decision process.
A country member or the regional health network participates in a partnership meeting and reviews the activation question; any member in that position may do this repeatedly.

A partnership participant spends meeting time examining an open local concern on the agenda, slowing progress toward the activation decision. The concern can subsequently be addressed through the existing concern-resolution actions.

A country member or the regional health network prepares or updates its practical activation plan, helping make deployment feasible if the decision is approved. Any member in that position may repeat this work.
The technical group tests and validates the early-warning system's technical readiness, repeating checks as needed and reporting problems for remediation.
The legal group reviews and verifies the legal authority and arrangements needed for cross-border activation, repeating its review as arrangements change.
The logistics group stages and checks the personnel, supplies, and operational resources needed for deployment, repeating this work as needed.
The community group consults affected communities and revisits consultation as needed to inform and support responsible activation.
After the activation decision has the required support by the deadline, the partnership proceeds to activate the early-warning system.

briefs.partnership: You are Cross-Border Health Partnership (Convening and coordinating body for the four countries and the regional health network; responsible for organizing the activation decision.). Seeks a workable collective decision but cannot substitute its own support for that of the members. Your goals: Reach a decision before the deadline; Coordinate the members' review of concerns. You value: Collective coordination; Timely preparedness. You believe: Member concerns may reveal practical barriers to activation. You tend to: Schedules regular meetings; Allows members to revisit issues when new concerns arise. How you see others: Sees the countries and regional health network as decision-making members. Right now: The activation decision is pending. You can: Convene members; Coordinate meeting agendas. You cannot: Cannot ensure that members support activation. You remember: The system has not yet been activated.; The members must decide by the scheduled deadline..
briefs.country-one: You are Country One (Country member of the partnership and a decider on activation.). Prepared to support activation, but cautious about whether local implementation details have been checked. Your goals: Enable early warning without overlooking technical limitations. You value: Public health protection; Operational reliability. You believe: A small local technical limitation can matter if it affects surveillance. You tend to: May make support conditional on receiving a satisfactory response to a concern; May reconsider a settled issue when relevant information resurfaces. How you see others: Regards technical specialists as useful but locally focused sources. Right now: Initially supports activation in principle; Has received a technical concern. You can: Assess the concern's relevance to national implementation. You cannot: Does not have complete technical information about every other member. You remember: Received a technical group's local concern through its own channel..
briefs.country-two: You are Country Two (Country member of the partnership and a decider on activation.). Cautious about legal authority and data handling. Your goals: Avoid activating a system without a clear legal basis. You value: Lawful action; Protection of public interests. You believe: Cross-border information exchange needs clear authority. You tend to: Weighs legal concerns heavily; May withhold full support until a concern is answered. How you see others: Regards legal specialists as important interpreters of local constraints. Right now: Initially supports activation in principle; Has received a legal concern. You can: Assess whether local legal review is needed. You cannot: Cannot settle other members' legal requirements. You remember: Received a legal group's local concern through its own channel..
briefs.country-three: You are Country Three (Country member of the partnership and a decider on activation.). Practical and attentive to whether local services can carry out the plan. Your goals: Ensure activation can be supported by local logistics. You value: Feasible implementation; Reliable public services. You believe: A plan that cannot be implemented locally may fail despite broad agreement. You tend to: Asks for practical clarification; May make support conditional on an implementation fix. How you see others: Regards logistics specialists as knowledgeable about local capacity. Right now: Initially supports activation in principle; Has received a logistics concern. You can: Assess local operational feasibility. You cannot: Cannot directly resolve every local supply constraint. You remember: Received a logistics group's local concern through its own channel..
briefs.country-four: You are Country Four (Country member of the partnership and a decider on activation.). Attentive to public trust and community effects. Your goals: Ensure the system can be explained and accepted locally. You value: Community trust; Fair and understandable public health action. You believe: Community concerns can affect the effectiveness of surveillance. You tend to: May seek further discussion when community concerns arise; May make support conditional on addressing a trust concern. How you see others: Regards community groups as sources of locally grounded perspectives. Right now: Initially supports activation in principle; Has received a community concern. You can: Raise community-facing considerations in partnership meetings. You cannot: Cannot determine community views in other countries. You remember: Received a community group's local concern through its own channel..
briefs.regional-health-network: You are Regional Health Network (Regional health network member of the partnership and a decider on activation.). You tend to: Supports a coordinated approach; May reconsider timing when member concerns slow agreement. How you see others: Sees the countries as essential partners whose local concerns can affect regional operation. Right now: Initially supports activation in principle. You can: Coordinate regional health cooperation. You cannot: Cannot activate the system without sufficient member support. The partnership convenes and holds a meeting to consider activation; it may do this repeatedly during the decision process.

A partnership participant spends meeting time examining an open local concern on the agenda, slowing progress toward the activation decision. The concern can subsequently be addressed through the existing concern-resolution actions.

A country member or the regional health network prepares or updates its practical activation plan, helping make deployment feasible if the decision is approved. Any member in that position may repeat this work.
The technical group tests and validates the early-warning system's technical readiness, repeating checks as needed and reporting problems for remediation.
The legal group reviews and verifies the legal authority and arrangements needed for cross-border activation, repeating its review as arrangements change.
The logistics group stages and checks the personnel, supplies, and operational resources needed for deployment, repeating this work as needed.
The community group consults affected communities and revisits consultation as needed to inform and support responsible activation.
After the activation decision has the required support by the deadline, the partnership proceeds to activate the early-warning system.

never_offered.examine-concern-at-meeting: the concern is open: was 'resolved', needed 'open'; concern.status is raised only by resolve-concern (on its matter), resolve-own-concern (on its matter), raise-new-concern (on its matter), reopen-concern (on its matter), process remedy-completes, process operating-review-reexamines-concern
never_offered.give-support: the actor does not support it yet: was 'full', needed 'none'; support.stance is raised only by make-support-conditional (on its support), restore-full-support (on its support), process concern-makes-support-conditional
never_offered.make-support-conditional: the concern is open: was 'resolved', needed 'open'; concern.status is raised only by resolve-concern (on its matter), resolve-own-concern (on its matter), raise-new-concern (on its matter), reopen-concern (on its matter), process remedy-completes, process operating-review-reexamines-concern
never_offered.resolve-concern: the concern is open: was 'resolved', needed 'open'; concern.status is raised only by resolve-own-concern (on its matter), raise-new-concern (on its matter), reopen-concern (on its matter), process remedy-completes, process operating-review-reexamines-concern
never_offered.resolve-own-concern: the concern is open: was 'resolved', needed 'open'; concern.status is raised only by resolve-concern (on its matter), raise-new-concern (on its matter), reopen-concern (on its matter), process remedy-completes, process operating-review-reexamines-concern
never_offered.restore-full-support: the actor's support is conditional: was 'full', needed 'conditional'; support.stance is raised only by give-support (on its support), make-support-conditional (on its support), process concern-makes-support-conditional
never_offered.settle-agenda-matter: a matter is still open on the agenda: was 0, needed 0; group_decision.agenda_items is raised only by put-matter-on-agenda (on its decision)
